teaser: Small releases are easier to review, easier to reverse and easier to learn from.
author: administrator
body:
Large changes hide uncertainty. Small changes expose it quickly. When the unit of delivery is narrow, testing becomes cheaper and feedback arrives while the context is still fresh.

Prefer visible progress

Ship one complete improvement, verify it, then move to the next. The same principle works for software, documentation and content.

A blog is a good place to document those increments: what changed, what was learned and what should happen next.
title: Shipping small improvements
